items.title: Decisions, architecture & delivery plan
items.goal: Before any application code exists, the team works from written records of the architecture, data model, UX structure, security and compliance baselines, test and AI-evaluation strategy, infrastructure plan and delivery order. Every PRD *open* question has an owner and its own decision issue, so nothing is settled silently inside an implementation PR.
prd: Overview → AI role, users, no sign-in in the MVP → decided
Technical architecture → layer table (frontend, backend, hosting, search, AI access, monitoring, testing) → decided and proposed
Data model (suggested) → 17 core tables and the job-version + model-version score key → suggested
Security (suggested) → 6 controls for a portal with no sign-in → suggested
Data, privacy & compliance → PDPA table, Risk 1 (no sign-in), fair employment → decided / at risk
Goals → MVP quality bar (≥ 90% fields, ≥ 80% top-5, EN and ZH separately) → decided
UI design → screen list and design rules → decided (screens) / suggested (rules)
Open questions → six items for the real-data release → open
exit: Every record in `docs/decisions/` and `docs/plans/` is merged and linked from this epic
Each of the six PRD open questions has a decision issue labelled `needs-decision`, or an explicit written deferral
No record settles a PRD open question; each one names the decision it is waiting on
Phase 1 tasks can start without any undocumented architectural assumption
outOfScope: Application code, migrations, designs or tests — those belong to phases 1 onward
Deciding the AI provider, the paid plans, the backup policy, the duplicate rule, the real-data date or the metric targets. The PRD lists these as open; this epic only records and routes them
Anything in the PRD non-goals (real data, email, backups, duplicate detection, client/candidate logins, external sources, Manatal migration, autonomous AI decisions, OCR, Teams/WhatsApp alerts)

items.title: The team builds from one written architecture and data-model record
items.story: As a recruiter sponsor, I want the technical shape of the portal written down and agreed before code is written, so that the MVP is delivered by mid-December 2026 without rework caused by unrecorded assumptions.
ac: Given a new contributor, when they read `docs/decisions/adr-0001-architecture.md`, then they can name which code may touch Supabase, where AI calls run, and why the browser never reaches the database.

Given the 17-table data model, when a schema task starts, then `docs/decisions/adr-0002-data-model.md` already states each table's purpose, its owning migration and the score key (candidate × job version × model version).

Given the AI provider is not chosen, when any AI code is planned, then `docs/decisions/adr-0003-ai-provider.md` states the provider-agnostic contract every AI call must satisfy and lists the decision as open.
prd: Technical architecture → How it fits together → suggested
Data model (suggested) → 17 tables, match-score key → suggested
AI governance → the dev team picks the AI provider → decided (which provider: open)
Integrations → AI model provider → MVP, provider still to decide

items.title: Write ADR-0001: application, data and AI boundaries
items.what: Record the architecture the PRD suggests as a decision record the whole backlog can cite: Next.js App Router on Vercel `sin1`, Supabase Postgres + private Storage in `ap-southeast-1`, server-only data access, API routes for AI work, `after()` for background re-scoring, and a database view (not a cron job) for delay status.
scope: `docs/decisions/adr-0001-architecture.md` with context, decision, consequences and rejected alternatives
The trust boundary: browser → Next.js server → Supabase/AI, and why the publishable key is never used for data
Where each PRD main flow runs (seeding, opening a job, saving a job, searching, delay status)
Which PRD layer choices are *decided* and which are *proposed*, so later tasks know what they may revisit
exclusions: Folder-level code layout — that is the scaffold task E01-S01-T01
done: `docs/decisions/adr-0001-architecture.md` exists and covers all five PRD main flows
Every layer in the PRD technical-architecture table appears with its decided/proposed status
The record states the rule that no browser code may import `src/server` or reach Supabase directly
verify: git diff --name-only   # docs only, no app code
markdown links resolve to files that exist

items.title: Write ADR-0002: the 17-table data model and its invariants
items.what: Turn the PRD's suggested 17-table model into a decision record: each table's purpose, its key columns, the migration that will create it, and the invariants that later tasks must not break.
scope: Table-by-table purpose and owning migration, mapped to the E03 migration tasks

Invariants: match scores keyed to candidate × job version × model version; recruiter overrides stored separately from parsed fields; every AI output row joins to `ai_runs`; UTC storage with Singapore display
Which tables the MVP needs and which exist only for the real-data release (consent, retention, last activity)
Where the skill mirrors live so `supabase-db` stays the mechanics reference
exclusions: Index and extension choices beyond naming pgvector and PGroonga
done: All 17 PRD tables appear with purpose, MVP-or-later, and owning migration task key
The four invariants above are stated as rules, each with the PRD line it comes from
Any table the PRD names but the MVP does not populate is marked as such
verify: every table name matches the PRD data-model table exactly

items.title: Write ADR-0003: AI provider decision brief and provider-agnostic contract
items.what: The PRD leaves the AI provider to the dev team and it is not chosen. Record the criteria, the shortlist and — most importantly — the contract every AI call must satisfy so that no code depends on a provider, and write the decision up as open with an owner.
scope: Decision criteria from the PRD: Simplified Chinese quality, cost, and where data is processed (PDPA overseas transfer)
The provider-agnostic contract: Vercel AI SDK, schema-validated structured output, model id and version recorded on every run, a separate embedding provider if the text provider offers none
What the MVP needs from a provider: direct PDF reading for Chinese fallback, multilingual embeddings, structured JSON
Status: open. Names the decision owner slot and what unblocks it
exclusions: Choosing a provider — this task must not settle it
done: `docs/decisions/adr-0003-ai-provider.md` states the decision as **open** and never names a chosen provider
The contract section lists every requirement app code may assume, and nothing provider-specific
The record links the tasks blocked on this decision
verify: the record contains no provider brand name as a decision

items.title: Every PRD open question has an owner and a decision issue
items.story: As a product owner, I want every undecided item tracked in one place with an owner and a decision point, so that no implementation PR quietly settles a question that is mine to answer.
ac: Given the PRD lists six open questions, when I open `docs/decisions/open-questions.md`, then each one shows its status, owner slot, what unblocks it, and the issue that will decide it.
Given an item is open, when a task depends on it, then that task carries the `needs-decision` label and names the open question.
Given a question is answered, when the register is updated, then the answer is recorded with its date and the issues it unblocks.
prd: Open questions → six items (pre-real-data requirements, paid plans, backups, duplicate rule, real-data date, metric targets) → open
Pipeline tracking → default stage limits → approved in the PRD, to be confirmed with the owner before seeding
UI design → review queue and name prompt → implied by requirements, not in the PRD screen list

items.title: Write the open-questions register and decision log
items.what: Create the single register of everything not yet decided: the six PRD open questions, plus the three repo-level confirmations the skills call out (default stage limits, the review-queue screen, Vercel Hobby's non-commercial terms). Each entry names what is blocked and which issue decides it.
scope: `docs/decisions/open-questions.md` with one row per question: status, owner slot, what unblocks it, blocked issues, deciding issue
The six PRD open questions, quoted from the PRD, unchanged
The three repo confirmations: stage default limits (E08-S02-T03), CV review-queue screen (E02-S04-T07), Vercel Hobby commercial use (E01-S04-T01)
A short rule for contributors: an open question is never settled inside an implementation PR
exclusions: Creating the decision issues — they already exist in this backlog and are linked, not duplicated
done: All six PRD open questions and the three repo confirmations appear, each linked to its `needs-decision` issue
No entry records an answer that the product owner has not given
The register states that MVP build is not blocked by the six PRD questions, which all belong to the real-data release

items.title: The UX structure is agreed before any screen is designed
items.story: As a recruiter, I want the portal's screens, navigation and main journeys mapped before anyone draws them, so that the nine MVP screens hang together instead of being designed one at a time.
ac: Given the PRD screen list, when I read `docs/ux/screen-inventory.md`, then every screen shows its purpose, its key elements, its phone-width behaviour and the design task that will draw it.
Given a recruiter's day, when I read the flows, then 'find candidates for a job', 'move a candidate and record my name' and 'clear today's overdue list' are each mapped end to end across screens.

Given two screens are implied by the requirements but absent from the PRD screen list (the CV review queue and the typed-name prompt), when the inventory is written, then both are marked as needing the product owner's confirmation.
prd: UI design → MVP screens table (9 screens) → decided
UI design → design rules (AI suggestion label, non-colour-only status, Noto Sans SC, phone width, name prompt) → suggested
CV processing → requirement 2, review queue → proposed

items.title: Write the screen inventory, navigation map and core recruiter flows
items.what: Map the information architecture before pen.dev work starts: the nine PRD screens plus the two implied ones, the navigation between them at desktop and phone width, and the three core recruiter journeys.
scope: `docs/ux/screen-inventory.md`: per screen — purpose, key elements from the PRD, entry points, phone-width behaviour, owning design task
`docs/ux/flows.md`: source-and-shortlist for a job; move a candidate with the typed-name prompt; clear the overdue dashboard
Navigation model: what is in the primary nav on desktop and what collapses on a phone
The five PRD design rules restated as constraints every screen design must show
exclusions: Any `.pen` file or visual design — that is E02
done: All nine PRD screens plus the review queue and name prompt appear with purpose and owning design task
The three flows each name every screen and state change they cross
The two implied screens are flagged for product-owner confirmation, not assumed
verify: every screen in the PRD table appears in the inventory

items.title: Security and compliance baselines are written before any code
items.story: As the agency director, I want the security and privacy position of a portal with no sign-in written down and its risks accepted explicitly, so that we know exactly what must change before real CVs are loaded.
ac: Given the MVP has no sign-in, when I read `docs/security/baseline.md`, then every control the PRD suggests is listed with the task that implements it and the test that proves it.
Given PDPA applies from the real-data release, when I read `docs/compliance/baseline.md`, then each PDPA obligation shows its MVP position and what the real-data release must add.
Given Risk 1, that anyone with the link can see every CV, when the risk register is written, then it records the risk as accepted for fictional data only and names the two cheapest fixes.
prd: Security (suggested) → six controls → suggested
Data, privacy & compliance → PDPA table (protection, consent, retention, overseas transfer, access & correction, breach notification) → decided / proposed / at risk
Data, privacy & compliance → Risk 1: no sign-in, accepted for the MVP → decided
Fair employment → Workplace Fairness Act end-2027; pregnancy, caregiving, disability, mental health not yet ignored → noted

items.title: Write the security baseline for a public, sign-in-less MVP
items.what: Record the security position the whole backlog inherits: the six PRD controls, the public-repo rules, and what each implementation task must prove. This is the checklist `security-check` reviews against.
scope: `docs/security/baseline.md`: secret handling, server-only data access, RLS with no public policies, private bucket with signed URLs, AI route rate limits and spend cap, typed-name recording
Public-repo rules: no secrets, no sample-data Blob URLs, no real personal data in issues, docs, tests or commits
The exposure model: the MVP URL is effectively public; what that means for uploads, AI routes and logs
A control → implementing task → proving test table
exclusions: Sign-in design — that is the real-data release (E15)
done: All six PRD security controls appear with an implementing task key and a proving test
The public-repo rules restate the Blob store as seed-source-only with no URL committed
The record names what must change before real CVs are loaded and links E15
verify: no secret, key or Blob base URL appears in the diff

items.title: Write the PDPA and fair-employment compliance baseline and risk register
items.what: Record the compliance position: what PDPA requires from the real-data release, what the MVP must already be designed for, how fair-employment rules bind scoring today, and the accepted risks.
scope: `docs/compliance/baseline.md`: PDPA protection, consent (7-day reminder, 14-day deletion), retention (12 months, 30-day warning), overseas transfer, access and correction, breach notification (500 people, 3 calendar days)
Fair employment: the attributes scoring must ignore; nationality and language only with a written reason; the Workplace Fairness Act attributes not yet covered, recorded as a revisit before end-2027
Model AI Governance Framework: which practices the MVP already follows through `ai_runs`, evidence quotes and the suggestion-only rule
Risk register: Risk 1 (no sign-in) accepted for fictional data; Risk 2 (old CVs) resolved; what each becomes at the real-data release
exclusions: Implementing consent, retention or deletion — real-data release (E14)
done: Every PDPA row in the PRD appears with its MVP position and its real-data requirement
The fair-employment section lists the ignored attributes exactly as the PRD decides them, and records the four Act attributes that are not yet covered as an open revisit
Risk 1 is recorded as accepted for fictional data only, naming the two cheapest fixes
verify: no real personal data appears anywhere in the diff

items.title: Quality is defined before it is built
items.story: As a recruiter who will grade the AI in December, I want the quality bar, the test strategy and the accessibility standard agreed now, so that the go/no-go decision rests on evidence we planned for rather than whatever we happened to measure.
ac: Given the PRD quality bar, when I read `docs/plans/ai-eval-plan.md`, then the answer-key format, the scoring method, and the separate EN and ZH bars (≥ 90% fields, ≥ 80% top-5) are all fixed before any prompt is written.
Given a logic task, when its plan is written, then `docs/plans/test-strategy.md` already says which layer tests it and which behaviours are test-first.

Given the dashboard and pipeline board must work at phone width, when a screen is built, then `docs/plans/accessibility-standard.md` states the keyboard, contrast, `lang` and overflow rules it must meet.
prd: Goals → MVP quality bar → decided
AI governance → requirement 4, recruiters grade EN and ZH separately → decided
Non-functional requirements → Testing: Vitest, Playwright, AI quality script → proposed
UI design → design rules 2, 3 and 4 (non-colour-only status, Noto Sans SC, phone width) → suggested
Non-functional requirements → Devices: desktop and mobile browsers → decided

items.title: Write the test strategy record
items.what: Fix the testing contract the whole backlog inherits: the four layers, the test-first list, fixture rules, frozen Singapore time, and which CI gate runs what.
scope: `docs/plans/test-strategy.md`: unit (Vitest), DB integration (local Supabase), e2e (Playwright desktop + phone), AI quality (eval)

The test-first list: working days, limit hierarchy, delay status, guarantee dates, must-have cap, redaction, evidence checks, total years, override merge, gap rules, search fusion, eval scoring, spend cap, env parsing, typed-name validation
Fixture rules: fictional only, no Blob access in unit or DB tests, no network in unit tests, explicit holiday fixtures
Per-area minimum proof table, and which gate blocks a merge
exclusions: Writing any test or test harness (E01-S01-T03)
Deciding a coverage percentage — the strategy is explicit that there is no coverage gate
done: All four layers appear with tool, location, command and what runs against
The test-first list matches the behaviours the PRD makes rules about
Each MVP area has at least one 'must prove' line
verify: every command named matches the script names in CLAUDE.md

items.title: Write the AI evaluation plan and answer-key format
items.what: Settle how the PRD quality bar is actually measured before any prompt exists: the answer-key file format, how a parsed field counts as correct, how top-5 agreement is computed, and how EN and ZH are graded separately.
scope: `docs/plans/ai-eval-plan.md`: bar (≥ 90% fields, ≥ 80% top-5), EN and ZH scored separately against the same bar
Answer-key format: keyed by file SHA-256, fictional content only, committed under `eval/answer-key/`, with a `verified` flag so unverified entries are excluded
Field-accuracy rules: which fields count, how normalisation and near-misses are treated, how a missing field scores
Top-5 agreement: what the recruiter ranking is compared against and how ties are handled
Cost control: how often the eval runs and roughly what a run costs
done: The plan states a single unambiguous rule for field correctness and one for top-5 agreement
EN and ZH grading is specified separately with the same bar
The answer-key format is fixed, keyed by SHA-256, and excludes unverified entries from the bar
The plan records that this scoring method is *proposed* in `ai-eval` and is being confirmed here
verify: no real personal data or Blob URL in the diff

items.title: Write the accessibility and responsive standard
items.what: Fix the accessibility and phone-width rules every screen must meet, so they are designed in rather than retrofitted. The PRD requires desktop and mobile browsers, non-colour-only status and a Simplified Chinese font.
scope: `docs/plans/accessibility-standard.md`: semantic HTML, labelled inputs, visible focus, full keyboard operation including stage moves, `aria-live` for async results, contrast from the tokens
Phone width (390 px): dashboard and pipeline board fully usable, tables collapse to cards, filters in a sheet, no horizontal page scroll
Chinese text: `lang="zh-Hans"`, Noto Sans SC in the stack, CSS truncation only, long-name cases
Delay status: always a word or icon plus colour, with the `aria-label` pattern
How each rule is checked: Playwright assertion, unit test, or design review
exclusions: Adding an axe dependency — that is E02-S05-T02, which this standard specifies
done: Every PRD design rule that concerns access or device width appears as a checkable rule
Each rule names how it is verified (test, assertion or review)
The phone-width overflow rule is stated as an assertable condition
verify: each rule names a verification method

items.title: Infrastructure and delivery order are planned
items.story: As the delivery lead, I want the environments, the env var inventory, the free-tier limits and the build order written down, so that the team can run phases in parallel where it is safe and knows what the free tiers will do to us.
ac: Given three environments (local, preview, production), when I read `docs/plans/infrastructure.md`, then each one names its Supabase project, its Vercel target and its env vars by name only.
Given the free tiers, when I read the plan, then each limit from the PRD table appears with its effect and the response we have chosen.
Given the phase structure, when I read `docs/plans/delivery-plan.md`, then the critical path, the parallel tracks and the definition of done are explicit.
prd: Environments & delivery (suggested) → one repo, preview per PR, 2 Supabase projects, CI applies migrations → suggested
Free-tier limits and risks → six limits with suggested responses → suggested
Non-functional requirements → uptime 99.5% best effort, backups none in MVP → at risk / decided
Release plan → MVP by mid-Dec 2026 → decided

items.title: Write the infrastructure plan, env var inventory and free-tier runbook
items.what: Record the environment map, the complete env var inventory by name, and the operational responses to every free-tier limit the PRD lists — including the weekly keep-alive that stops Supabase Free pausing the MVP between review sessions.
scope: `docs/plans/infrastructure.md`: local / preview / production → Supabase project, Vercel target, migration source
Env var inventory: names, which environment holds them, server-only vs public, and which are secrets. **Names only, never values**
Free-tier responses: Hobby non-commercial, weekly keep-alive, no backups (re-seed), 500 MB / 1 GB / 50 MB caps, one region and daily cron, no uptime guarantee
Recovery: migrations plus seed are the backup plan; what a rebuild costs in time and AI calls
exclusions: Creating the Vercel project or setting any variable (E01-S04-T01)
Choosing paid plans — that is a PRD open question
done: Every env var the MVP needs is listed by name with its environment and secret status, and no value appears
All six PRD free-tier limits appear with the chosen response
The recovery procedure names the exact commands the re-seed will use once they exist

items.title: Write the delivery plan: phases, critical path and definition of done
items.what: Record the phase order this backlog is built on: what each phase delivers, which phases sit on the critical path to mid-December 2026, which tracks can run in parallel, and the definition of done every task shares.
scope: `docs/plans/delivery-plan.md`: the phases P0–P12, each with its epics, entry condition and exit condition
Critical path: foundation → data → CV processing → matching → pipeline → launch, with the design-system and AI-governance tracks marked as parallel
Parallel tracks and their synchronisation points (for example: designs must land before the screen build tasks in the same phase)
Definition of done for a task: acceptance criteria proven by named tests, verification commands green, review passed, completion summary recorded in the plan's Outcome section
exclusions: Re-planning the backlog itself — this records the phase structure already on Project 4
Estimating in days or assigning people
done: Every phase P0–P12 appears with its epics and exit condition
The critical path and the parallel tracks are both explicit
The shared definition of done matches the 'Definition of done' section every task issue carries
verify: every phase on Project 4's Phase field appears in the plan
